page: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an Arm-based instance powered by first-generation AWS Graviton processors, built on 64-bit Arm Cortex-A72 microarchitecture. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides 8 physical CPU cores mapped directly to 8 dedicated vCPUs operating at a fixed frequency of 2.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring persistent network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, and no hardware GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput reflecting its first-generation Arm design. Synthetic stress-ng testing reports single-core performance of 1,491.99 and multi-core output of 11,904.08, placing raw synthetic compute in the mid-range. Real-world execution speeds trail significantly, illustrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 410.0 and a multi-core score of 2,143.0. Memory subsystem throughput is constrained, achieving 23.51 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 8.88 GB/sec write bandwidth. Static web serving reaches 2.41 GB/sec, while in-memory operations measure 4.24 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a budget-friendly environment for scale-out Arm architectures. The a1.2xlarge offers qualitative infrastructure cost advantages for non-latency-sensitive workloads capable of running on Arm64 instructions, though it trades off single-threaded speed and memory transfer throughput compared to modern x86 or newer Graviton generations. It is suited for basic web serving fleets, development environments, containerized microservices, and continuous integration pipelines compiling multi-architecture Arm binaries.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is a first-generation Arm-powered instance delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores based on the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture clocked at 2.3 GHz. Managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 16.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and does not bundle local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes. In synthetic testing, stress-ng achieves 11,904.08 multi-core points, though Geekbench scores of 410.0 single-core and 2,143.0 multi-core demonstrate limited per-thread computing density. Memory write throughput reaches 8.88 GB/sec, with Redis operations measuring 4.24 million operations per second. With an entry-level compute profile and balanced core count, a1.2xlarge serves scale-out Arm web serving, continuous integration builds, microservices, and lightweight development tasks.
